title: The Rain, 2012
logline: Fifteenth January. The first Rain from the motel desk. Four panels of the glass door at 3 AM and the hum line under all of them. Not yet a Sunday; the line is already new.

panels.composition: The Driftwood Motel's glass door from the night desk, 3 AM. Rain. The lot's sodium light. WOOD's shoulder at the frame's edge. The hum line beneath.

image.prompt: a motel lobby's glass door seen from the night desk at 3 AM with rain on the glass and one sodium light in the lot, a clerk's shoulder at the frame edge, razor-sharp ink, a flat unbroken line running beneath the panel

panels.composition: Same. The rain harder. A car's headlights sweeping the lot, not stopping.

image.prompt: the same motel glass door with rain harder and a car's headlights sweeping across the lot without stopping, a flat unbroken line running beneath the panel

panels.composition: Same. The rain. Nothing. The bell on the desk in the foreground, unrung.

image.prompt: the same glass door with rain, a desk bell in sharp foreground focus unrung, a flat unbroken line running beneath the panel

panels.composition: Same. Dawn gray-green through the rain. The sodium light clicking off. Held.

image.prompt: the same glass door at dawn with rain and gray-green light, the lot's sodium lamp just switched off, a flat unbroken line running beneath the panel, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Four times the same door. The line new. The hum under all of it.
